items.title: A module admitting a left dual in the monoidal category of modules is finite projective
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that a module with a left dual in the monoidal category of modules is finite projective, identifies the dual with the module of homomorphisms into the ring and computes the evaluation in terms of that identification, and the proof is a 28-line argument built on a lifting of the unit of the duality. It writes the two duality identities, lifts the unit along a map from a finite free module onto the given module, draws the resulting commutative diagram and reads off from it a factorisation of the identity of the given module through the finite free module, which exhibits it as a direct summand and hence projective; the same diagram then gives the identification of the dual with the Hom module and the formula for the evaluation. The lifting step and the diagram chase that produces the splitting are the substance, and both are displayed.
